To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The proposed analog VLSI implementation is a low power solution for feature extraction in a speech recognition system, and (2) The proposed feature extraction scheme combined with HMMs and LDA can achieve a word error rate (WER) of 6.1% (for the TI-DIGITs database) which is comparable to the state of the art in digital speech recognition.

the VLSI chip performs feature extraction in real-time, that the feature set is suitable for speech recognition, and that the VLSIC based speech recognizer performs as good as or better than a software recognizer.
the VLSI implementation has a low power consumption, that it can be used as a real time front-end of a recognizer and that it improves recognition performance.

we are able to achieve a recognition rate of about 90% with our system, using 16 MFCC coefficients (13 cepstral coefficients and 3 energy coefficients), a 3-state HMM and LDA.
our VLSI implementation is able to achieve a 5.8% error rate on a subset of the TI-DIGTS database.

we have successfully developed and implemented an analog VLSI front end for speech recognition and that our results on a speech recognition system based on the analog VLSI auditory front end are promising.

the proposed front-end can be implemented with low power and low area.

a front-end based on the human auditory system is a viable alternative to conventional front-ends for speech recognition.
